patch.value: Recovery commands rendered on Windows are not paste-safe in PowerShell: $(...) and backticks expand inside CommandLineToArgvW double quotes

Recovery commands (`restore_with`, `suggested_retry`, next-step hints) are rendered by `quoteCommandArg` / `renderPmCommand` in `src/core/shared/command-line.ts`, used across 41 source files. On `win32` the helper follows CommandLineToArgvW quoting, which is correct for cmd.exe and CreateProcess, as settled in pm-b24b. PowerShell, however, expands `$var`, `$(...)` and backticks inside double quotes. An argument such as a tracker path `C:\trackers\$(Start-Process calc)` therefore expands when a user pastes the command into PowerShell. The argument comes from the user's own `--pm-path` or `PM_PATH`, so this is low risk, but recovery text should be paste-safe in the shell the agent actually uses.

CodeRabbit raised it on PR #1635 for `tests_omitted.restore_with`. It applies to every rendered recovery command, so it needs one shell-dialect decision instead of a per-call-site patch.

Decide the recovery-command shell dialect on win32 (cmd/CreateProcess, PowerShell, or a declared dialect field); quoteCommandArg renders arguments containing $, backtick, ( or ) so that pasting into the declared shell never expands them; unit tests cover win32 cmd and PowerShell rendering of a tracker path containing $(...) and a backtick; existing cmd/CreateProcess round-trip tests stay green
A recovery command rendered on Windows can be pasted into the declared shell without expanding $, $(...) or backticks in any argument.
